description: Gold-cased and cut with a sunburst rune, left by a Runemane. It is still carrying out old orders.
lore: The two who brought the first one in could not agree, that night at the fire, on what they had done. One of them used the polite word and said released. The other would not take either of the trade's two words and kept saying, instead, that they had taken a fitting off a building.

He had the better of it and everybody knew. [[monsters/rune_lion|The guardian]] is Made: it never fell and was never anywhere, only remembering that pooled with nothing to be, thickened, and stood up at a door. A stone is the last hard piece of somebody, the bottom of a long forgetting, and there is not supposed to be a bottom to a thing that was never filled. Yet here it lies in its gold case, warm as any of them, the sunburst still lit in the cut of it, doing what it plainly does: set it in a blade and every fifth strike, unasked and without fail, it puts itself in front of the next blow. It is not protecting you. It is standing where it was told to stand.

They left it at the meadow fire and went, which is what people do with a thing they cannot price. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] has had it in her apron since. Somebody there made the obvious comparison out loud, in the tone people use when they think they are being kind — the last one on a rota that lapsed everywhere else. She said the lion was left with orders and she was left with people, and that these are not the same thing, and got up to see to the wood.
gm_notes: This is the batch's one Made-leaves-a-stone record; the other Made stones must not re-run the argument. The Runemane record belongs to Gunnar's floor plan and Wendell's honesty about the room, so neither appears here. The trade has settled nothing and should stay unsettled: no answer is canon yet. Solveig's line is the §8 rule stated as a refusal, and it is the closest she comes to defending the watch.
